'''Darko Miličić''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Дарко Миличић}}, {{IPA|sr|ˈdarko ˈmilit͡ʃit͡ɕ}}; born 20 June 1985) is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player. He is {{height|m=2.13}}, and played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) from 2003 to 2012. Nicknamed "'''the Human Victory Cigar'''" for only playing in blowout wins or losses,<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Dorsey |first=Jesse |title=The Top Human Victory Cigars in the NBA |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1017544-the-top-human-victory-cigars-in-the-nba |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref> Miličić is the [[List of oldest and youngest National Basketball Association players|fifth youngest player]] and the youngest foreign player to have played in the NBA, the youngest player to have played in an NBA Finals game, and the youngest player to win the NBA championship.

Miličić was selected by the [[Detroit Pistons]] as the second overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]; he was chosen after number one pick [[LeBron James]] and ahead of other future NBA superstars including [[Carmelo Anthony]], [[Chris Bosh]], and [[Dwyane Wade]]. Selected with a high draft pick, Miličić never played at the level expected of him in the NBA and is widely considered a [[draft bust]]. While he won an NBA championship with the Pistons in 2004, Miličić never received significant playing time with the team and was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2006. Following stints with the Magic, [[Memphis Grizzlies]], and [[New York Knicks]], Miličić was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in 2010 and signed a four-year contract with the team that summer. After being released by Minnesota in 2012, he played one regular-season game for the [[Boston Celtics]] later that year before being released. Miličić announced his retirement from the NBA in 2013; he retired with career averages of 6.0 points and 4.2 rebounds per game.

In international play, Miličić played for the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]].

==Early life==
Miličić's parents are Milorad and Zora. During the [[Yugoslav Wars]], when Miličić was not yet 10, he heard a news report in which his father was named as one of several Serbian soldiers killed in action; however, a few minutes later, the newscaster indicated some of the soldiers, including his father, had been incorrectly included as killed. His father ultimately survived the wars.<ref name=Borden>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/feature/story/_/id/20211833/nba-bust-darko-milicic-finds-success-back-home-serbia |title=Finding Darko |first=Sam |last=Borden |work=ESPN.com |date=August 2, 2017 |access-date=August 2, 2017}}</ref> His parents' families hail from Janj near [[Šipovo]] in [[Bosanska Krajina]].<ref name=telegraf88873>{{cite news|title=Miličić - srpski vitez opevan u osmercu (VIDEO)|url=http://www.telegraf.rs/sport/88873-milicic-srpski-vitez-opevan-u-osmercu-video|access-date=16 July 2015|work=Telegraf.rs|date=25 February 2012|language=sr}}</ref> His sister, Tijana, is a volleyball player.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2003-03-31-darko-focus_x.htm | work=USA Today | title=Serbian teen lost in King James' shadow | first1=David | last1=DuPree | date=April 2, 2003 | access-date=May 1, 2010}}</ref>

Miličić played his first youth basketball in [[KK BFC Beočin|BFC Beočin]] until the [[NATO bombing of Yugoslavia]] that lasted from 24 March to 10 June 1999, when he was forced to take a break.<ref name=talk>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oX9SJWulU2U |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/oX9SJWulU2U| archive-date=2022-04-27 |url-status=live|title=VIVALDI TALKS #24: Darko Miličić, bivši košarkaš i preduzetnik|last=MokrogorskaTV|date=21 April 2022 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref> After that, Miličić played for the basketball club Sports World from Novi Sad, which is also a basketball school, where he became a dominant figure and received interest from bigger teams.<ref name="talk"/> He played club basketball with his friend Nemanja Jokić, the older brother of [[Nikola Jokić]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Jenkins |first=Lee |date=2017-02-08 |title=The Joker: Nikola Jokic gets serious in Denver |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/02/08/nikola-jokic-denver-nuggets-the-joker-serbia-darko-milicic |access-date=2023-05-22 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

At age 14, Miličić started playing basketball with the Serbian team [[KK Hemofarm|Hemofarm's]] junior team.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/vault/2003/03/03/338924/darko-milicic-this-17-year-old-7-footer-may-be-the-nbas-no-2-draft-pick|title=Darko Milicic This 17-year-old 7-footer may be the NBA's No. 2 draft pick|first=Ian|last=Thomsen|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=March 3, 2003}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story?id=1586626|title=Hemofarm Vrsac says it has Piston through 2009|date=July 28, 2003|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was later called up from the junior team before being drafted by the NBA's Detroit Pistons in 2003.<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pistonpowered.com/2010/09/13/myth-detroit-pistons-picking-darko-milicic-over-carmelo-anthony-with-the-no-2-pick-in-the-2003-nba-draft-was-an-avoidable-blunder/|title=Myth: Detroit Pistons picking Darko Milicic over Carmelo Anthony with the No. 2 pick in the 2003 NBA Draft was an avoidable blunder|last=Feldman|first=Dan|date=September 13, 2010}}</ref>

==NBA career==
===Detroit Pistons (2003–2006)===
[[File:Darko Milicic Pistons.jpg|thumb|left|Miličić (left) in 2006]]
The Detroit Pistons chose Miličić with the second overall pick in the 2003 NBA draft.<ref name="auto1" /> Unlike most teams with high draft choices, the Pistons were a good team that had made the Eastern Conference Finals [[2002–03 NBA season|the season before they drafted Miličić]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Keith|last=Langlois|title=What If: Yes, the Pistons drafted Darko No. 2. No, drafting Carmelo wouldn't have guaranteed more titles – or any|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/what-if-yes-pistons-drafted-darko-no-2-no-drafting-carmelo-wouldnt-have-guaranteed-more-titles|website=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2020|access-date=September 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417095455/https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/what-if-yes-pistons-drafted-darko-no-2-no-drafting-carmelo-wouldnt-have-guaranteed-more-titles|archive-date=April 17, 2020}}</ref> The [[NBA draft]] rules had to be changed to allow Miličić to be drafted.<ref>{{Cite web|title=What If: Yes, the Pistons drafted Darko No. 2. No, drafting Carmelo wouldn't have guaranteed more titles – or any|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/what-if-yes-pistons-drafted-darko-no-2-no-drafting-carmelo-wouldnt-have-guaranteed-more-titles|access-date=2021-10-16|website=Detroit Pistons|language=en}}</ref> The Pistons held the second overall draft pick because of a 1997 [[trade]] that had sent [[Otis Thorpe]] to the [[Vancouver Grizzlies]].<ref name=chosenones>{{cite news|last1=Windhorst|first1=Brian|title=The chosen ones|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/page/2003-draft-history-1/an-oral-history-2003-lottery-draft|access-date=20 February 2015|website=ESPN.com|date=23 June 2013}}</ref> Miličić saw limited playing time during his first season with the Pistons, but became the youngest player to appear in an NBA Finals game (18 years and 356 days) and won an NBA championship five days later when the Pistons defeated the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the [[2004 NBA Finals]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/darko_milicic/bio.html Darko Milicic biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091201151356/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/darko_milicic/bio.html |date=2009-12-01 }}. NBA.com. Retrieved on October 30, 2009.</ref> During Game 5, Miličić broke his right hand after [[Brian Cook (basketball)|Brian Cook]] committed a shooting foul, resulting in him requiring surgery that sidelined him from the Pistons for eight weeks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 17, 2004 |title=Pistons' Milicic has hand surgery |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/pistons-milicic-has-hand-surgery-1.487786 |access-date=October 31, 2025 |work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref>

Pistons team president [[Joe Dumars]] repeatedly stated that Miličić would play a big part in the team's future, but he did not see a large increase in playing time during his second season. However, on April 19, 2005, Miličić had his best game as a Piston, playing 30 minutes as a starter and recording 16 points, five rebounds, and three blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Montalbo |first=Ike |title=Darko Milicic's 16 Greatest Games As a Pro...So Far |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/519026-darko-milicics-16-greatest-games-as-a-pro-so-far |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f25MPT65Hog |title=Darko Milicic's Best Game as a Piston (16 Points, 5 Rebounds, 3 Blocks) |date=2021-07-29 |last=Ryan Van Dusen |access-date=2025-09-24 |via=YouTube}}</ref> This was one of two games Miličić started in Detroit, with the other being the next game after where he played 30 minutes while recording nine points, three rebounds, and a block. Miličić never saw this amount of playing time as a Piston again and has been quoted on numerous occasions as attributing his slow development on his lack of playing time: "I've said it 10,000 times, the best way for me to improve is to play. All the work in practice and individual workouts can only help me so much".<ref>{{cite news| url=https://archive.boston.com/sports/articles/2005/06/17/pistons_milicic_is_still_waiting_watching/| title=Pistons' Milicic is still waiting, watching | last=Lage | first=Larry | work=[[The Boston Globe]]|agency=Associated Press| date=June 17, 2005|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref>

After [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]]'s departure, [[Flip Saunders]] was hired as head coach of the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|first=Liz|last=Robbins|title=Brown Leaves the Pistons; Knicks Leave a Door Open|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/07/20/sports/basketball/brown-leaves-the-pistons-knicks-leave-a-door-open.html|website=The New York Times|date=July 20, 2005|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Pistons Name Flip Saunders as Head Coach|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/saunders_050721.html|website=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2005|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref> Under Saunders, Miličić still averaged only 5.6 minutes per game, and received significant playing time only in blowout wins or blowout losses for the Pistons.<ref name=":5" /> Miličić's lack of playing time in Detroit was frequently highlighted in publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=No mercy: Pistons pound short-handed Knicks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260119018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504170458/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260119018|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 4, 2018|website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|date=January 20, 2006|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=No need for Pistons to hastily trade Darko|url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/news/no-need-for-pistons-to-hastily-trade-darko/article_2beb0a4f-e8bd-5a11-8353-0150ed35b2f7.html|website=The Oakland Press|date=January 22, 2006|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite web|first=Patrick|last=Hayes|title=Darko Milicic: Pistons should've drafted Dwyane Wade or Carmelo Anthony|url=https://www.mlive.com/fullcourtpress/2010/01/darko_milicic_pistons_shouldve.html|work=MLive|date=January 8, 2010|access-date=September 16, 2020}}</ref> In the 96 games he played as a Piston, he only scored a total of 152 points and averaged 1.6 points and 5.8 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/DET/players.html|title=Detroit Pistons Players|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2006–2007)===
On 15 February 2006, just prior to the NBA's [[NBA All-Star Weekend|All-Star weekend]], Miličić was traded, along with [[point guard]] [[Carlos Arroyo]], to the [[Orlando Magic]] for [[Kelvin Cato]] and a first-round pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] ([[Rodney Stuckey]]).<ref>
{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2332021 | title=Pistons get Cato, first-round pick for Darko, Arroyo | agency=Associated Press | publisher=[[ESPN]] | date=2006-02-22}}</ref>

During a game against the [[New York Knicks]], Miličić played 32 minutes and finished with 13 points and seven rebounds, which were season highs for him, while leading the Magic in minutes for that game. Miličić averaged 2.4 blocks per game in his first 20 games as a member of the Magic. In round 1 of the [[2007 NBA playoffs|2007 playoffs]], Orlando faced off against Miličić's old team, the Detroit Pistons, who swept Orlando in four games. During the series, Miličić increased his scoring to 12.3 on 58.8% shooting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/darko_milicic/career_stats.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070630211523/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/darko_milicic/career_stats.html|url-status=dead|title=NBA.com Darko Milicic career stats|website=[[NBA.com]]|archive-date=June 30, 2007}}</ref> When his rookie contract expired in the 2007 offseason, Orlando made him a qualifying offer, but the team withdrew that offer on 3 July 2007 and made Miličić an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2925284|title=With Lewis agreement, Magic withdraw Darko offer|date=July 3, 2007|last=Ford|first=Chad|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2007–2009)===
[[File:Darko Milicic 2008 Grizzlies (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Miličić (left) in 2008]]
On 12 July 2007, the first day of free agency, Miličić was signed by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] to a three-year, $21 million contract.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2933472 Milicic, Grizzlies agree on three-year deal] July 11, 2007</ref> He hurt his [[Achilles tendon]] practicing with the Serbian national team in the 2008 offseason but was available to start at the beginning of the season. Miličić began the 2008–09 season starting at power forward, but was moved to the bench due to poor play. He regained his starting job as his play steadily improved in early December 2008. Miličić's progress was set back by an injury on 26 December 2008, against the Indiana Pacers when he broke a knuckle on his right hand during the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3795876|title=Milicic to miss 4-6 weeks with broken knuckle|date=28 December 2008|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Miličić's time with the Grizzlies was one of the low points of his career; he did not want to play for the team, he suffered an injury, and the team was not performing well.<ref name="hoopshype.com">{{cite web|url=https://hoopshype.com/storyline/whatever-happened-to-darko-milicic/|title=Whatever Happened to Darko Milicic - HoopsHype}}</ref> Miličić's wife would recall that he would punch the walls of his house in anger after coming home from games.<ref name=Borden/> During a game against the [[Houston Rockets]] in early December 2008, he even deliberately ripped his jersey in frustration (the jersey was later autographed by him and sold at an auction).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/milicic_torn_jersey_on_auction_block-081209.html|title=Darko Milicic's torn jersey from Grizz v. Rockets win to go on online auction block|website=Memphis Grizzlies}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/memorable-jersey-tears-nba-history/story?id=50976025|title=More memorable jersey tears from NBA history|date=7 November 2017|website=ABC News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SguBaDSLFd0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/SguBaDSLFd0| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=darko-rips-his-jersey|last=theassociation|date=10 December 2008 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QbiMohwBSBo |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/QbiMohwBSBo| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=[Darko Miličić ]darko-rips-his-jersey|last=Darko Miličić|date=14 March 2017 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tyJnsO-95X8 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/tyJnsO-95X8| archive-date=2021-12-12 |url-status=live|title=darko rips his jersey|last=TheAlassondro|date=7 February 2012 |via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2009–2010)===
On 25 June 2009, Miličić was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] for [[Quentin Richardson]] and cash considerations.<ref>
{{cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/news/milicictrade090625.html | title=Knicks Trade For Former No. 2 Overall Pick Milicic | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2009-06-25 | access-date=2009-06-28}}</ref> On 17 December, Miličić said that he planned to leave the NBA and return to playing basketball in Europe the following season.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/knicks/count_darko_out_pbz7MTegxNv38e272IVXDO | title=Darko plans European return as he can't get off Knicks bench | date=2009-12-17 | access-date=2009-12-17 | work=New York Post | first=Marc | last=Berman}}</ref> In the eight games he played for the Knicks, Miličić averaged 2.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Darko Miličić 2009-10 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/milicda01/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2010–2012)===
[[File:Darko Milicic cropped.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Miličić in April 2010]]
On 17 February 2010, Miličić was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with cash considerations for [[Brian Cardinal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Acquire_Darko_Milicic_from_New_York_2010_02_17.html |title=Wolves Acquire Darko Milicic from New York |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-02-17 |access-date=2010-02-18}}</ref> The Timberwolves agreed to re-sign Miličić for four years and $20 million on 1 July. [[David Kahn (sports executive)|David Kahn]] said that Darko was "like manna from heaven."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Craggs|first1=Tommy|title=Darko Milicic Is Bread From God, And Other Crazy Things David Kahn Believes|url=http://deadspin.com/5588342/darko-milicic-is-bread-from-god-and-other-crazy-things-david-kahn-believes|access-date=14 March 2015|work=Deadspin|date=15 July 2010}}</ref>

The 2010–11 Minnesota season was Miličić's best statistically; in interviews, he looked back on that time period fondly relative to the rest of his time in the NBA.<ref name="hoopshype.com" /> He averaged 8.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.0 blocks per game, finishing the season fifth in the league in blocks per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2171/darko-milicic|title=Darko Milicic Stats|publisher=ESPN|access-date=February 9, 2020}}</ref> Miličić had his best games on 19 November, when he scored 23 points, 16 rebounds and six blocks against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301119016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101122073754/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301119016|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 22, 2010|title=Kobe Bryant, Matt Barnes key Lakers' rout of Wolves|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 19, 2010}}</ref> and on 14 December, when he had a career-high 25 points and 11 rebounds against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301214009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101220231854/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=301214009 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 20, 2010 |title=Warriors end 7-game slide as Monta Ellis and Reggie Williams combine for 60 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=December 14, 2010}}</ref>

Miličić began the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011-12 season]] as the Timberwolves' starting center. On 20 January 2012, he scored a season-high 22 points and seven rebounds against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320120012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120124023248/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320120012|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 24, 2012|title=Kevin Love's 3 gives Minnesota the win after Ricky Rubio's tying 3-pointer|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=January 20, 2012}}</ref> However, he would see his playing time diminish as the season went on. On 12 July, Miličić was waived by the Timberwolves under the league's [[amnesty clause]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-waive-darko-milicic |title=Wolves Waive Darko Milicic |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2012-07-12 |access-date=2012-07-12}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2012)===
In September 2012, Miličić signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-sign-milicic|title=Celtics Sign Milicic|website=Boston Celtics}}</ref> In October 2012, during the Celtics preseason exhibition games in Europe, Miličić averaged 2.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 3.0 blocks per game, with Celtics head coach [[Doc Rivers]] stating that Miličić could become a starter in order to rest [[Kevin Garnett]] early.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-10-11 |title=Forsberg: Darko Milicic settling in with Celtics |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8492120/darko-milicic-settling-boston-celtics |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> During the NBA preseason, Miličić played one game against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on 15 October, where he recorded six points, three rebounds, and a block in seven minutes before injuring his wrist.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Game Preview: Celtics at 76ers (preseason) {{!}} Boston Celtics |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/game_preview/game-preview-celtics-76ers-preseason |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> On 21 November 2012, the Celtics released Miličić at his request so that he could attend to personal matters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-waive-milicic|title=Celtics Waive Milicic|website=Boston Celtics}}</ref> Miličić's final game ever was on 2 November, a 99–88 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] where he recorded a rebound, two turnovers, and a foul. This was the Celtic's second game of the regular season, and it was the fourth game that Miličić played during the entire season, playing only five minutes for that game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1420875-darko-milicics-release-great-timing-for-the-boston-celtics|title=Darko Milicic's Release: Great Timing for the Boston Celtics|first=Randolph|last=Charlotin|website=Bleacher Report|date=November 24, 2012}}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
In June 2013, Miličić announced that he had retired from the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Moore|first=Matt|date=23 June 2013|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/22508472/darko-milicic-says-hes-done-with-the-nba|access-date=26 June 2017|title=Darko Milicic says he's done with the NBA|work=CBS News}}</ref> He retired with career averages of 6.0 points and 4.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2014/09/22/nba-bust-darko-milicic-retires-to-try-a-new-sport/|title=NBA bust Darko Milicic retires to try a new sport|first=John|last=DeMarzo|date=September 22, 2014}}</ref> In September 2014, it was revealed that Miličić had retired from professional basketball in order to pursue a kickboxing career.<ref>{{cite news|title=Darko Miličić stavio tačku: zbogom NBA karijero, dobar dan kik-bokse!|url=http://www.nbaserbia.com/vesti/9700/darko-milicic-stavio-tacku-tacka-na-nba-karijeru-postaje-kik-bokser|access-date=22 September 2014|work=nbaserbia.com|language=sr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141026081557/http://www.nbaserbia.com/vesti/9700/darko-milicic-stavio-tacku-tacka-na-nba-karijeru-postaje-kik-bokser|archive-date=26 October 2014|url-status=usurped|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

=== Legacy ===
As of February 2023, Miličić is [[List of oldest and youngest NBA players|the fifth youngest player]] to have played in the NBA,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/20-youngest-players-to-ever-debut-in-nba|title=20 Youngest Players To Ever Debut in NBA|date=January 2, 2023|website=clutchpoints.com}}</ref> the youngest foreign player to have played in the NBA, the youngest player to have played in an NBA Finals game, and the youngest NBA champion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thepostgame.com/blog/dish/201409/report-darko-milicic-retiring-professional-basketball-pursue-kickboxing|title=Report: Darko Milicic Retiring From Pro Basketball To Pursue Kickboxing|website=ThePostGame.com|access-date=2020-01-28|archive-date=2020-01-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128102151/http://www.thepostgame.com/blog/dish/201409/report-darko-milicic-retiring-professional-basketball-pursue-kickboxing|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-17 |title=The youngest players to win an NBA title |url=https://hoopshype.com/gallery/youngest-players-nba-title-champions/ |access-date=2023-02-05 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref> After having been selected with the second overall pick in the 2003 NBA Draft, Miličić failed to play at the level expected of him in the NBA and is known as one of the worst draft choices in the history of the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/us-sports/darko-milicic-confessions-from-the-biggest-draft-bust-in-nba-history/news-story/b8f69d370c7c76af1af691b5e468fc86|title=NBA bust: 'I'll f**k up the team'|date=March 15, 2017|website=www.heraldsun.com.au}}</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/nba-draft-busts-2015-6|title=WHERE ARE THEY NOW? The biggest NBA Draft busts of all time|first=Scott|last=Davis|website=Business Insider}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/749269-darko-milicic-the-biggest-missed-opportunity-or-biggest-draft-bust|title=NBA Draft: Is Darko Milicic the Biggest Draft Bust Ever?|first=Mark David|last=Smith|website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> Miličić himself has questioned whether the Pistons made the right move by drafting him.<ref name="auto" /> The Pistons passed over future NBA stars Carmelo Anthony, Chris Bosh, and Dwyane Wade to select Miličić. In June 2011, Mark David Smith of ''[[Bleacher Report]]'' wrote, "The Pistons missed a huge opportunity when they picked Darko. Carmelo, Wade or Bosh could've helped put Detroit over the hump after the 2004 championship season. The thought of one of these superstars with that Pistons team is scary; it could've potentially made them one of the best dynasties in all of sports history".<ref name="auto1" />

==National team career==
Miličić played for the [[Serbia men's national under-16 basketball team|FR Yugoslavia U16 national team]] that won a gold medal at the European Cadet Championships in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.nba.com/draft2003/profiles/MilicicDarko.html|title=NBA.com: Prospect Profile: Darko Milicic|website=archive.nba.com}}</ref>

In 2006, Miličić led [[Serbia and Montenegro national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro]] at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. Serbia and Montenegro had decided to replace their aging superstars—who had led the team to a gold medal finish in the previous [[2002 FIBA World Championship]]—with young blood. Miličić led the team in rebounds (56) and blocked shots (17) and was second on the team in scoring (16.2 ppg) and assists (11) through six games. In Serbia and Montenegro's sixth and final game against [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]], Miličić matched up against [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] All-Star [[Pau Gasol]] and finished with 18 points, 15 rebounds, and three blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Darko Milicic profile, FIBA World Championship 2006 |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/38624/sid/3507/tid/92330/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820092106/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/38624/sid/3507/tid/92330/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_World_Championship/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 20, 2019 |access-date=2024-10-21 |website=FIBA.COM}}</ref>

During an interview following a 68–67 overtime loss to [[Greece national basketball team|Greece]] at [[EuroBasket 2007]], Miličić made vulgar remarks to the media in his native language. He referred to the referees with expletives and threatened to engage in various sex acts with their female relatives.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metacafe.com/family-filter/off/?return_url=%2Fwatch%2F808311%2Fdarko_milicic_swears_and_threatens_referees_english_sub%2F|title=Metacafe - Online Video Entertainment Metacafe - Online Video Entertainment|last=metacafe.com|website=Metacafe|access-date=2019-01-25|archive-date=2018-07-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180716224006/http://www.metacafe.com/family-filter/off/?return_url=%2Fwatch%2F808311%2Fdarko_milicic_swears_and_threatens_referees_english_sub%2F|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{YouTube|jaKk8vBiCPw|Miličić' angry comments after Serbia-Greece (Serbian language)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/2016/10/6/16040946/darko-milicic-nba-banana-boat-week-c275d98d242a|title=Darko Milicic Should Have Been a Cult Hero|first=Mark|last=Titus|date=October 6, 2016|website=The Ringer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadspin.com/the-picturesque-word-stylings-of-darco-milicic-296948|title=The Picturesque Word Stylings Of Darco Milicic|website=Deadspin|date=6 September 2007 }}</ref> He received a $13,770 fine from [[FIBA]] and his outburst was heavily criticized by [[Memphis Grizzlies]] general manager [[Chris Wallace (basketball)|Chris Wallace]] and head coach [[Marc Iavaroni]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/olybb/news/story?id=3009568|title=FIBA fines Milicic $14K for Euro referee outburst|date=7 September 2007|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Post-NBA activities==
=== Kickboxing career ===
Miličić had a stint in [[kickboxing]] during 2014. On 18 December 2014, he had his official debut in kickboxing under the [[World Association of Kickboxing Organizations|WAKO]] rules in his hometown Novi Sad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wakopro.org/en/news/what-an-amazing-month-for-wako-pro-december-2014/5aa1d4e4-b20e-4e22-8d40-83388936ce84|title=What an amazing month for Wako Pro December 2014!!!|website=WAKOPRO}}</ref> Miličić lost that fight by second round [[Technical knockout|TKO]] from Serbian kickboxer Radovan Radojčin from [[Senta]], Serbia.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://muaythaivojvodina.rs/print.php?news.234|title=MILJAN K-1 PRVAK EVROPE - Klub borilačkih sportova ''VOJVODINA''|website=muaythaivojvodina.rs}}</ref>

=== Professional basketball return attempt ===
On 19 May 2015, it was announced that Miličić had agreed to come back from retirement and start playing professional basketball again with [[KK Metalac Valjevo|Metalac Farmakom]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] and the [[ABA League]] after the season was over. The announcement was made by Boško Đukanović, the club's president, and later confirmed by Miličić himself.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|date=19 May 2015|title=Miličić potpisao za Metalac: Uželeo sam se košarke, Đukanović ima velike ambicije|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:548892-Milicic-potpisao-za-Metalac-Uzeleo-sam-se-kosarke-Djukanovic-ima-velike-ambicije|work=[[Večernje novosti]]|language=sr}}</ref> However, Miličić later changed his mind.<ref name=":1">{{cite news|date=12 September 2015|title=Miličić odustao od igranja za Metalac!|language=sr|work=Sportske.net|url=http://www.sportske.net/vest/kosarka/milicic-odustao-od-igranja-za-metalac-237269.html|access-date=15 September 2015}}</ref>

=== Farming ===
Miličić works as a farmer in his native Serbia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/1091477|title=Former 1st-rounder Milicic now living as a farmer|first=William|last=Lou|website=theScore.com|date=2 September 2016 }}</ref> {{as of|2017|8}}, Miličić owned and operated an [[apple]] orchard of about {{convert|125|acre}}, with plans to purchase more land and also grow [[Cherry|cherries]].<ref name=Borden/>

=== Amateur basketball career ===
In September 2019, Miličić joined [[KK I Came to Play|I Came to Play]] in his hometown of Novi Sad.<ref name=":2">{{cite news|author1=Austin Kent|date=17 September 2019|title=Darko Milicic to return to professional basketball|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/darko-milicic-to-return-to-professional-basketball/|access-date=7 October 2019}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite news|date=17 September 2019|title=Darko Milicic back to action|work=Eurohoops.net|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/935951/darko-milicic-back-to-action/|access-date=7 October 2019}}</ref> He debuted with the team on 6 October in a 78–50 victory against [[KK Futog]], scoring two points and handing out several assists before leaving the game with a minor shoulder injury.<ref name=":4">{{cite news|author1=Aleksandar Latas|date=6 October 2019|title=Veliki Kambek - Miličić se vratio na teren i pregazio Futog sa 28 razlike|language=sr|work=Blic Sport|url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/darko-milicic-ponovo-igra-kosarku-pobedio-futog/vl2x9k9|access-date=7 October 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On 23 May 2009, Miličić married Zorana Markuš.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Radojković|first1=M.|title=Adrijana uživala u srpskoj kuhinji|url=http://www.blic.rs/Zabava/Vesti/94066/Adrijana-uzivala-u-srpskoj-kuhinji|access-date=14 March 2015|work=blic.rs|date=25 May 2009|language=sr}}</ref> They have a daughter (b. 2009) and two sons (b. 2010 & b. 2012).<ref name="zorana17">{{cite news|last1=Čanović|first1=Anastasija|title=NESVAKIDAŠNJA SUPRUGA DARKA MILIČIĆA Sve tetovaže sam posvetila deci!|url=http://www.blic.rs/zabava/vesti/nesvakidasnja-supruga-darka-milicica-sve-tetovaze-sam-posvetila-deci/6dtt2v5|access-date=4 December 2017|work=blic.rs|date=25 January 2017|language=sr}}</ref> His wife is a fashion designer<ref name="zorana17" /> and the sister of deceased Serbian criminal Marko Markuš.<ref>{{cite news|title=SKUPA KOLA, JAHTE, POZNATI PRIJATELJI Ovako je živeo Marko Markuš, žestoki momak Novog Sada likvidiran u sačekuši|url=http://www.blic.rs/vesti/hronika/skupa-kola-jahte-poznati-prijatelji-ovako-je-ziveo-marko-markus-zestoki-momak-novog/32bvhs9|access-date=30 November 2017|work=blic.rs|date=30 November 2017|language=sr}}</ref>

In 2010, Miličić paid for a trip and treatment in China for five Serbian children with [[Batten disease]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Zvezdana protiv Batena|url=http://zvezdana.rs/LP.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131208203353/http://zvezdana.rs/LP.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=2013-12-08|language=sr}}</ref> In April 2011, inspired by the actions of former NBA player [[Metta Sandiford-Artest|Ron Artest]], Miličić auctioned up his 2003–04 championship ring, his championship belt gifted to him by [[Rasheed Wallace]],<ref>{{cite news |last=Enlund |first=Tom |date=December 4, 2004 |title=Former Pistons get their hands on title belts |url=http://www.jsonline.com/story/index.aspx?id=280867 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013142654/http://www.jsonline.com/story/index.aspx?id=280867 <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=October 13, 2007 |access-date=February 23, 2008 |publisher=JS Online}}</ref> raffle tickets, and an all-expenses paid trip to an NBA Finals game to raise money for children with Batten disease.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-04-07 |title=Darko auctioning 2004 title ring, belt for charity |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6302231 |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lutz |first=Jeff |date=2011-04-07 |title=Darko to Auction Ring for Charity |url=https://www.vintagedetroit.com/darko-to-auction-ring-for-charity/ |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=Vintage Detroit Collection |language=en-US}}</ref>

Miličić is a supporter of the [[Chetniks|Ravna Gora movement]],<ref>{{cite news|title=SPREM'TE SE: Darko Miličić šeta novog četnika|url=http://www.kurir.rs/sport/kosarka/spremte-se-darko-milicic-seta-novog-cetnika-clanak-1473013|access-date=16 July 2015|work=Kurir.rs|date=22 July 2014|language=sr}}</ref> and has tattoos of [[World War II]] [[Chetniks|Chetnik]] leaders [[Nikola Kalabić]]<ref>{{cite news|title=TETOVIRAO KALABIĆA: Miličić krenuo Čičinim stopama|url=http://www.kurir.rs/tetovirao-kalabica-milicic-krenuo-cicinim-stopama-clanak-934873|access-date=14 March 2015|work=kurir.rs|date=13 August 2013|language=sr}}</ref> and [[Momčilo Đujić]] on his stomach,<ref>{{cite news|title=Poraz Miličića na debiju u ringu|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/borilacki/kikboks.php?yyyy=2014&mm=12&dd=18&nav_id=938029|access-date=14 March 2015|work=b92.net|date=18 December 2014|language=sr}}</ref> and [[Draža Mihailović]] and [[Branko Bogunović|Brane Bogunović]] on his back.<ref>{{cite news|title=I batine su za ljude: Miličić u ringu|url=http://www.vesti-online.com/foto-galerija/457570/i-batine-su-za-ljude-milicic-u-ringu|access-date=14 March 2015|work=vesti-online.com|language=sr}}</ref> In late 2013, Miličić expressed his support for far-right politician [[Vojislav Šešelj]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former NBA star Dragan Milicic expressed support for Vojislav Seselj|url=http://inserbia.info/today/2013/11/former-nba-star-dragan-milicic-expressed-support-for-vojislav-seselj/|access-date=14 March 2015|work=inserbia.info|date=2 November 2013|language=sr}}</ref>

A folk song was made in his honour by the [[Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Serb]] duo ''Žare i Goci''.<ref name="telegraf88873" /> In March 2024, Miličić stated that he is a fan of [[KK Crvena zvezda|KK Crvena Zvezda]] and is a member of the Assembly for KK Crvena Zvezda on the Jao Mile [[podcast]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kowicki |first=Lukas |date=2024-03-14 |title=Darko Milicic I didn't want to spoil my relationship with Crvena Zvezda, I barely follow the EuroLeague |url=https://basketballsphere.com/en/darko-milicic-i-didnt-want-to-spoil-my-relationship-with-crvena-zvezda-i-barely-follow-the-euroleague/ |access-date=2025-10-31 |website=Basketball Sphere |language=en-US}}</ref>
